Hi Julia — thanks for the redlines and clear summary. Short answers up front, then next steps: 

- Invoicing entity: Redwood Inference, Inc. (US-based) will issue invoices for the hosted service. We can provide the full remittance and entity details in a billing appendix.
- VAT/tax: For EMEA usage we can generate VAT invoices if you provide your VAT ID and billing entity; otherwise we typically apply gross billing and then support you on tax reclaiming. We also support reverse-charge handling where applicable — will need your legal to confirm VAT registration.
- Consolidated monthly invoices are supported; split invoicing by tranche is also possible but requires a contract note specifying invoice triggers (we can model as \"Invoice 50% at kickoff, 50% quarterly thereafter\" or monthly split).
- Minimum commit: by default, minimum commits are invoiced pro-rata over the initial term unless you request an up-front tranche. We can be flexible; include preferred cadence and we'll reflect that in the order form.

I'll loop in Karthik from commercial ops and David from finance to agree the precise wording and evidence required for tax handling.

Next steps: Karthik to propose invoice cadence options; David to confirm documentation we need (W-9/W-8/VAT cert). Suggest a short call tomorrow to close — are you available 10–10:30 PT?

Thanks,

Hi all,

Following Vanessa's note, here's a concise set of invoice cadence options we can propose to Acme legal/finance (we'll capture the chosen option in the order form pricing schedule):

Option A — Monthly consolidated invoice
- Single consolidated invoice at month end for all usage and commitment consumption.
- VAT invoicing applied based on provided billing entity and VAT ID.

Option B — Tranche-based billing
- Initial invoice for 50% of first commit at signature; remainder invoiced monthly across the term.
- Suitable if Acme requires upfront capacity allocation.

Option C — Prepaid commit (up-front)
- Full minimum commit invoiced at signature and applied as credit to monthly usage.

We also need to confirm how to handle any shortfall vs. minimum commit (invoice immediately vs. reconcile on month-end). Best practise: reconcile monthly and invoice shortfalls quarterly to reduce AP churn.

Can you confirm which option you prefer or if legal requires specific language around taxes/reverse-charge? I can draft the exact clause for the order form.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Julia/Karthik/Vanessa — quick finance note on tax evidence and docs we need to avoid invoice delays: 

- US customers: W-9 for entity validation (if invoiced by Redwood Inference, Inc.).
- Non-US/EU customers: VAT registration number + certificate for VAT invoice processing. If Acme requests reverse-charge, we need written confirmation and a valid VAT ID to apply zero-rated reverse charge.
- For certain EMEA entities, we may need a local tax registration copy to support VAT reclaim.

On minimum commit billing: if Acme wants to invoice monthly but pay minimum commit up-front, we should document that as a prepayment credit in appendix. If you choose reconciliation billing, we'll include a quarterly shortfall invoice clause (Net 30).

I will prepare a short appendix (billing appendix) with three checkbox options (monthly consolidated / tranche-based / prepaid commit) and a clear line describing which entity is invoiced and who is responsible for taxes.

I'll attach a template W-9 and the billing appendix draft for legal redline.
